## One-line Summary

SkillRL distills successful and failed trajectories into a hierarchical skill bank, then co-evolves that bank with a policy trained through SFT and GRPO.

## 1. Document Information

SkillRL: Evolving Agents via Recursive Skill-Augmented Reinforcement Learning. 2602.08234v1; first submitted 2026/02/09. The exact [local PDF](../papers/xia-2026-skillrl-evolving-agents-via-recursive.pdf) has 18 pages. Citations use 1-based PDF pages. Review covers the main method, cited experiments and limitations; no reproduction was run. [Author-linked project/code](https://github.com/aiming-lab/SkillRL) is provided for follow-up; implementation behavior was not audited.

## 2. Key Contributions

Uses compact general and task-specific guidance rather than retaining entire trajectories. Couples skill-conditioned policy learning to periodic expansion based on validation failures. It supplies a concrete predecessor and baseline for CoSkill, SkillForge, and SESA. [PDF p. 3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.08234v1#page=3) [PDF p. 4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.08234v1#page=4)

## 3. Methodology and Architecture

A teacher distills the initial bank and generates skill-augmented SFT demonstrations. General skills are always included; semantic retrieval selects task-specific entries. GRPO trains the solver. At validation epochs, weak categories trigger teacher synthesis from sampled failures and the existing bank. Algorithm 1 appends proposed skills, although the text also asks the teacher to refine ineffective entries; it does not train the teacher/editor itself. [PDF p. 3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.08234v1#page=3) [PDF p. 4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.08234v1#page=4) [PDF p. 5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.08234v1#page=5)

## 4. Key Results and Benchmarks

Table 1 gives Qwen2.5-7B ALFWorld success 89.9% versus the listed GRPO baseline 77.6%, and WebShop success 72.7% versus 66.1%; WebShop score is separately 85.2 versus 79.3. The GRPO row is marked as sourced from prior work, so the 12.3-point gap is not by itself a clean component-isolation experiment. Search evaluation covers seven QA datasets, with separate transfer claims from training on NQ/HotpotQA. [PDF p. 5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.08234v1#page=5) [PDF p. 6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.08234v1#page=6)

## 5. Limitations and Future Work

The skill bank is externally edited by a teacher, while the policy weights learn; this is not joint training of a meta-skill editing role. Teacher data, SFT initialization, and differing baseline provenance complicate causal attribution. Validation failures actively drive bank updates, so validation is part of development. Compression ratios should not be treated as end-to-end compute savings including the teacher. [PDF p. 4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.08234v1#page=4) [PDF p. 5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.08234v1#page=5) [PDF p. 6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.08234v1#page=6)

## 6. Related Work

[[feng-2026-coskill-joint-reinforcement]]; [[yang-2026-skillforge-evolving-verifiable-skills-for]]; [[fu-2026-self-play-meets-skill-evolution]]. Synthesis: [[concepts/procedural-self-improvement]] and [[overviews/self-improving-llm-agents]].

## 7. Glossary

SkillBank: general plus task-specific procedural memory. Cold-start SFT: teacher demonstrations teaching skill use. GRPO: group-relative policy optimization from sampled trajectory rewards.
